gloss: bushido; the way of the samurai

definitions.gloss: bushido; the way of the warrior; the samurai code of conduct
definitions.explanation: The moral code and ethical principles of the samurai class in feudal Japan, emphasizing loyalty, honor, discipline, and self-sacrifice. Also used in modern Japanese to refer to a spirit of fairness and integrity.

examples.japanese: {武士道|ぶしどう}の{精神|せいしん}を{学|まな}ぶ。
examples.english: To learn the spirit of bushido.

examples.japanese: {武士道|ぶしどう}では{名誉|めいよ}を{何|なに}より{大切|たいせつ}にした。
examples.english: In bushido, honor was valued above all else.

examples.japanese: {新渡戸稲造|にとべいなぞう}の『{武士道|ぶしどう}』は、{日本|にほん}の{道徳観|どうとくかん}を{海外|かいがい}に{紹介|しょうかい}した{名著|めいちょ}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: Nitobe Inazo's 'Bushido' is known as a masterwork that introduced Japanese moral values to the world.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
The concept of {武士道|ぶしどう} was codified and popularized through {新渡戸稲造|にとべいなぞう}'s 1900 book 'Bushido: The Soul of Japan,' written in English for a Western audience. Key virtues include {義|ぎ} (righteousness), {勇|ゆう} (courage), {仁|じん} (benevolence), {礼|れい} (respect), {誠|まこと} (honesty), {名誉|めいよ} (honor), and {忠義|ちゅうぎ} (loyalty).

In modern usage, {武士道|ぶしどう}{精神|せいしん} (bushido spirit) is invoked to describe fair play, perseverance, and integrity, often in sports and business.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {武士道|ぶしどう}{精神|せいしん} (the spirit of bushido)
- {武士道|ぶしどう}に{反|はん}する (to go against bushido)
- {武士道|ぶしどう}の{教|おし}え (the teachings of bushido)
